_comment: The onboarding tour and the hub's first-week checklist (src/ui/tour.js). Copy only: the anchors are CSS selectors tried in order (a [data-tour] attribute first, so a page can name its own anchor), and every checklist tick is DERIVED from the open film in tour.js by the item's id; a step or item with a `module` is left out while that module is switched off for everybody (plan-gate isDisabledEverywhere) — nothing here, and nothing about a tick, is stored. The steps walk every page in navigation.json order (the studio stages first, then the global pages), and a step with `admin: true` is shown only while the gate reports an admin; a hidden step keeps its index, so a stored step always names the same page. Only the tour's own place (which step, dismissed) is kept, in fms_tour_v1, and only when the reader clicks.

steps.title: Start with a real film
steps.body: The Dragon sample is a complete production — a screenplay, its scenes broken down, a schedule, a unit list and call sheets. Open it and every page of the studio has something on it to read, edit or delete.
steps.doneBody: The sample is open. Next, the story it was built from.

steps.title: Dashboard: your film’s home
steps.body: Continue picks up where you left off; the stage cards show what is next.

steps.title: Story: the idea, the logline, the beats
steps.body: Write the synopsis and tag its passages to the beats of a structure; the heatmap and the pacing notes are worked out from what you tag.

steps.title: Idea Vault: loose ideas and notes
steps.body: Park loose ideas and sticky notes here and copy them into the script later.

steps.title: Screenplay Writer: write the screenplay
steps.body: It formats as you type — slug lines, action, cues, dialogue — and keeps the page count honest. Every scene heading you write becomes a scene in the breakdown.

steps.title: Drafts: numbered versions
steps.body: Save numbered versions of the script and compare them.

steps.title: Scene Breakdown: what each scene needs
steps.body: Tag cast, props, vehicles and sound against each scene. The elements list, the schedule, the budget and the call sheets all read these tags, so nothing is typed twice.

steps.title: Visualize: shots and frames
steps.body: The shot list and the storyboard for each scene.

steps.title: Plan: locations and the calendar
steps.body: Your locations and the shoot calendar, in one place.

steps.title: Stripboard: scenes into shoot days
steps.body: Drag the strips into days. The day out of days, the Shoot Calendar and the call sheets follow the board.

steps.title: Reports: read from your scenes
steps.body: The one-liner, the sides, the daily production report and the equipment list, all read from your scenes.

steps.title: Budget: what the schedule costs
steps.body: The estimate reads the days off your stripboard and the rates off the Chennai tables, and every figure stays editable. Change a shoot day and the number here follows it.

steps.title: Cast and crew: everyone on the film
steps.body: Everyone on the film, in one list. Call sheets and the budget read from it.

steps.title: Shoot day: on the phone, on the set
steps.body: Today's scenes, biggest first, with who is called. Mark each one shot, part or dropped; the edit log reads those marks to say what is in the can and what is still owed.

steps.title: Call sheets: who, where, when
steps.body: A call sheet is a day's scenes plus the people called for them. Print one, or save it as a PDF to send to the unit.

steps.title: Edit log: what is in the can
steps.body: The cut’s word on each scene, read from the marks you made on the floor. The set’s answer is final here — this page never writes back to a shoot day.

steps.title: Deliverables: what leaves, and where it goes
steps.body: Picture, sound, text and legal, each with what a festival or a streamer asks for. The festival list carries the date each entry was last checked, so you can see what is stale.

steps.title: Library: around the studio
steps.body: Craft books, case studies and a film glossary, open whichever film you are on.

steps.title: Settings: how the studio works for you
steps.body: Your preferences, plan and backup, and this tour if you want it again.

steps.title: Plans: what each includes
steps.body: What each plan includes and what it costs, before you pay anything.

steps.title: Console: for admins
steps.body: People, plans, billing and invites. Only admins see this step.

invite.line: New here? Take a 2-minute tour of the studio.

checklist.label: First week
checklist.title: Find your way round
checklist.deck: A few things to try. Each one ticks itself off as you work on your film.
checklist._during: An item with `during: trial` is listed only while a trial that ends within the week runs, while a launch pass runs (it is not a plan chosen), or once a plan is bought (plan-gate.js entitlement() and currentPlan(); a year-long grandfathered trial, a grant or an ended trial list nothing), and ticks only when a plan is actually bought: derived, like the rest.
